subject: Post-call: volume bands, target $/1M tokens & pro-forma estimate
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ellen Park <ellen@auroraai.co>
Cc: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T14:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps (volume bands + target $/1M tokens)

Hi Ellen — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we can put a pro-forma estimate on paper for your procurement team.

What we covered (as I captured it)
- Expected monthly volume: baseline 1.2M tokens, burst up to ~6M in peak months. Preferred contract base band: 1M–3M and 3M–7M.
- Target unit economics: you mentioned aiming for ~USD $400–600 / 1M tokens for production-quality (low-latency) throughput.
- Primary workload: multi-turn customer assistant (avg context 600 tokens / session), batching-friendly traffic but with 95th percentile latency target ~250ms.
- Compliance: standard SOC2+IP whitelist; you may request audit log demo during procurement.

Immediate asks from our side
1) Confirm which band you want priced as the committed monthly minimum (1M, 3M, or 5M) — we can produce sliding pro-forma for each.
2) Confirm an initial budget range for procurement to evaluate (you mentioned the procurement playbook has a ~USD 10k–30k monthly bucket).
3) Any special billing terms (PO cadence, net30 vs net45) so we reflect that in the invoice estimate.

Attached: a quick pro-forma workbook (Aurora-token-proforma-v1.xlsx) and our pricing calculator export. The pro-forma models three scenarios: conservative (1M committed), standard (3M committed), scaled (5M committed) with quantization & batching assumptions.

If you’re ok, I’ll share the pro-forma with procurement and loop in your PO contact — propose a 30-minute follow-up on Wednesday to walk the numbers.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
T: 415-555-0134 | jordan.blake@redwood.ai

---
Attachment: Aurora-token-proforma-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet summary, 3 scenarios)

From: Ellen Park <ellen@auroraai.co>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T14:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (volume bands + target $/1M tokens)

Thanks Jordan — this matches my notes. A couple clarifications before I escalate to procurement: 

- Confirm that the $/1M tokens you show for the standard scenario assumes 8-bit quantization + batching. Is there a separate line for FP16? We need to show worst- and best-case unit cost to our finance team.
- For bands: initial ask is to price 1M committed with an option to top up month-to-month (we want the flexibility) — but please include the 3M and 5M committed scenarios for comparison.
- Procurement will want a short explanation of how burst capacity is billed (we prefer simple overage rules).

Procurement contact is procure@auroraai.co — please send the pro-forma plus an illustrative invoice for the standard (3M) and conservative (1M) options.

Can you send the two invoice mockups and a one-page note on assumptions? Happy to take the call Wednesday at 10am PT.

Ellen Park
Head of ML Ops, Aurora AI
ellen@auroraai.co

To: Ellen Park <ellen@auroraai.co>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-04T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps (volume bands + target $/1M tokens)

Ellen — thanks for the quick reply. I attached the redwood-pricing-calculator.csv export and included a short breakdown here so procurement has a clear line-item view.

Summary (three modeled scenarios)
1) Conservative — 1M committed, 600 avg tokens/session, modest batching
   - Assumed quantization: 8-bit int (Q8)
   - Modeled $/1M tokens: $680 (higher due to low commit + conservative latency SLO)
2) Standard — 3M committed, optimized batching (40ms queue window), Q8 + KV cache
   - Modeled $/1M tokens: $455
3) Scaled — 5M committed, aggressive batching + 4-bit quant path (Q4/8 hybrid)
   - Modeled $/1M tokens: $290

Burst/Overage approach
- Burst up to 150% of committed band billed at 1.2x standard $/1M rate; sustained excess beyond 150% triggers a temporary auto-scale recommendation and a review call.

Assumptions & line-items included in CSV
- GPU-hours allocated, average tokens/sec, caching savings (prefix reuse), batching latency targets, and model quantization path. We also include an illustrative invoice line for a monthly fixed fee (support & telemetry) if you want SLA-backed telemetry retention.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-calculator.csv (CSV export of the spreadsheet).

If you want, Jordan and I can produce two short invoice mockups (PDFs) for 1M and 3M scenarios and a one-pager assumptions doc. Jordan — should I produce the mockups now and send directly to procure@auroraai.co?

— Sergio
Sergio Alvarez | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: Pro-forma + illustrative invoices (1M & 3M)

Ellen / procurement team — forwarding the pro-forma and CSV export. Per Ellen's ask, attached are two illustrative invoice mockups and a short assumptions page.

What we included:
- Invoice A (conservative): 1M committed band, line-items for tokens, support, and telemetry retention; total estimated monthly: USD 11,800.
- Invoice B (standard): 3M committed band, optimized batching assumptions; total estimated monthly: USD 14,700.
- A one-page assumptions doc (inside Aurora-token-proforma-v1.xlsx) that explains quantization, batching windows, caching expectations, and burst billing rules.

Next steps:
1) Procurement: please confirm preferred committed band and PO cadence (net30/net45).
2) If accepted, we'll convert the selected invoice mockup into a formal quote and issue an SOW addendum (if you require a fixed-term commitment).
3) Jordan/Sergio to run a 30-minute walk-through Wednesday 10am PT — please confirm.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Jordan Blake | Enterprise AE, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai
